text:
Sam W: Heads-up — I repro'd a steady memory climb on MQA Llama-2 when rope scaling crosses 4096->8192. Not typical fragmentation: pages are being reallocated but not reused, looks like redundant page records in the KV index.

Aanya R: Interesting. Is this the same pattern as the earlier 'kv journal' issues or something new?

Sam W: Different. Journal sweep was about stale refs. This looks like duplicate allocations for the same KV slot during rekeying under MQA. Feed a long prompt (30k tokens) and watch resident set grow linearly even with sweep enabled.

Miguel: Can you paste the perf traces / pmap output?

Sam W: Here is a short extract from a reproduce run on a dev instance (condensed):

```
# token  rusage_kb  kv_pages_allocated  kv_index_entries
0        120MB      512                 512
2000     160MB      640                 512   <-- pages > index
4000     210MB      832                 512
8000     310MB      1200                512
```

Shows pages allocated > index entries (we see duplicates).

Linh: Which codepath ties to rope scaling? Is it during cache rearrange on sequence-length grow, or when we switch kernel tiling?

Sam W: It's triggered when rope exponent shifts (we hit a boundary), the KV transform that normalizes positions does a small compaction step. During that compaction we create a new page list but the old pointers aren't removed in the per-shard metadata if there is an interleaving async write. Race suspicion.

Aanya R: That fits with a race during the async dump -> compact -> swap. Do we have any failing assertions in debug builds?

Sam W: In debug builds it sometimes hits: "kv_index: duplicate_page_entry" but not consistently (timing). In release it silently accumulates.

Miguel: Any model differences? You said MQA Llama-2 — what about Mistral and Qwen?

Sam W: Mistral and Qwen (GQA variants) don't hit it on the same runs. Hypothesis: MQA uses a different per-token update path that does small in-place page creation to support interleaved kv writes, which interacts badly with our compaction. Qwen's page writer is more batched, so the race is masked.

Linh: Could this explain the odd GC spikes we saw in canary last week? Saw spikes when context balloons then drops and host OOM.

Sam W: Yes — OOMs match high-water marks when redundant pages double memory for long contexts.

Aanya R: Repro plan? We should capture a lock-free trace and a minimal reproducer to run under rr/TSAN.

Sam W: Steps I used:
1) Start dedicated dev node with debug kernel, perf events enabled.
2) Run long-chat script with alternating long prefixes and short completions hitting rope boundary. (script in gist: https://internal/gists/kv-rope-repro)
3) Collect /proc/<pid>/maps + kv debug dump at intervals.

I attached a tiny reproducer here (inline):
```
# pseudo-repro
for i in {1..100}; do
  send_prefix $(python gen_long_prefix.py --len $((4096 + (i%2)*4096)))
  send_short_completion
done
```

Miguel: I'll try TSAN on a smaller variant. Linh, can eng-infra spin a canary with the debug kv-index asserts enabled on a dedicated small pool? If we can reproduce CI-level we'd catch it earlier.

Linh: Yup — I'll queue a canary with kv-debug=1 and 30m retention. Tagging @devops-bot to create build.

devops-bot: Canary scheduled: canary/kv-rope-dup-1790123456 — 4xg5-small — logs retained 60m. Link: https://canary/internal/kv-rope-dup-1790123456

Aanya R: If TSAN repros, we should try a fix: make compaction use compare_exchange on shard->page_list or drain pending writers before swapping. Also add an invariant check that page_count == index_entries post-swap in debug.

Sam W: Agreed. I'll prototype a patch to add a short global compaction lock for the swap window and add the assert. If that reduces perf we can micro-opt it (compare_exchange per-shard).

Miguel: One more ask — can we add a lightweight metric to console: kv_redundant_pages and kv_peak_dup_ratio so we can alert on growth in prod?

Sam W: Good idea. I'll open a small ticket and add a console panel for the canary.

Aanya R: Thanks. If anyone sees similar on other models, drop logs here. Let's avoid a full rollback until we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:

Sam W: Will follow up with PR and perf numbers.
